mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate level is causally linked to higher S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days, as it reduces the cost of capital for corporations and increases the present value of future cash flows.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC for FEDFUNDS as a predictor of 20-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate rises above 2.0% in a 3-month period, it signals a tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in < 40% of triggered instances (FEDFUNDS > 2.0% for 3 months), or the Rank IC for the trigger condition is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and increase in nonfarm payrolls signals a strong labor market that boosts corporate earnings and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between UNRATE and PAYEMS does not produce a positive Rank IC (below 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 5-day return when UNRATE falls and PAYEMS rises is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of housing market expansion (HOUST > 1200 thousand units) and strong GDP (GDPC1 > 17000 billion), the S&P 500 experiences positive forward returns over the next 60 days due to robust consumer spending and business investment.
failure_condition: In periods where HOUST > 1200 and GDPC1 > 17000, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC for the joint condition is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts fall below 1100 thousand units, it signals a weakening housing market that reduces consumer confidence and business investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in < 40% of triggered instances (HOUST < 1100), or the Rank IC for HOUST as a predictor of 5-day returns is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts and increase in retail sales signals a shift in consumer spending patterns that boosts equity valuations due to strong retail performance offsetting housing weakness, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The interaction between HOUST and RSAFS does not produce a positive Rank IC (below 0.03) over any 3-year rolling window, or the average 20-day return when HOUST falls and RSAFS rises is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During periods of low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) and high payroll levels (PAYEMS > 145000 thousand), the S&P 500 experiences positive forward returns over the next 60 days due to robust corporate earnings and consumer spending.
regime_hint: low unemployment and strong payroll growth
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS > 145000, the 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC for the joint condition is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts is causally linked to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days, as it reflects strong consumer confidence and business investment.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for HOUST as a predictor of 5-day SPX returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
